paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. Since 22/11/2026, with 14 days of Kalshi collection, the market table shows both books side by side and the gap between them, in points. Under the dates the government announced on 01/07/2026, the first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027; the decree that convenes the voters has not yet been published.

**On 23/11/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, Polymarket pays 45.75, in the 17:05 UTC reading, and Kalshi 50.00, in the 17:10 UTC reading. In the 79 first-round lists with fieldwork ending between 09/10 and 17/11, from 7 pollsters, she is first in all of them, with 27% to 40%, and she leads in the 35 runoff matchups in which she was tested in that period, with 52% to 70%. The two most recent polls in the database are still YouGov's for Le HuffPost, with fieldwork from 12 to 17/11, and Ifop-Fiducial's for TF1-LCI, Le Figaro and Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 13 to 16/11. Two polls already published are not yet in this screen's counts, because the database that structures the lists has not yet included them: Ifop-Fiducial's for Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 2 to 4/11 (notice 10392), and wave 10 of Toluna Harris Interactive for M6, RTL and L'Express, with fieldwork from 18 to 19/11, whose notice (10393) is already on the Commission des sondages list. Le Pen's appeal against ineligibility at the Cour de cassation is due to be decided by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the win contract of both markets.** In the polls, he averages 18.3 across 34 lists from 6 pollsters with fieldwork ending between 24/10 and 17/11, and is among the top two in 73 of the 79 lists from 09/10 to 17/11; in the 12 runoff matchups in which he was tested in that period, he trails in all of them, with 30% to 39%. In the win contract, he is at 14.50 on Polymarket and 12.00 on Kalshi.

**David Lisnard is 2nd in the win contract of both markets and is not among the top two in any of the 40 poll lists in which he appears.** On Polymarket, he is at 20.75; at 15:30 UTC on 23/11, the series recorded 22.85, his highest price since the series began on 08/11/2026. On Kalshi, he is at 20.00. In the polls, he appears in 40 of the 79 lists from 09/10 to 17/11, from 7 pollsters, with 4% to 17%, and averages 9.5 across 26 lists from 6 pollsters with fieldwork ending between 24/10 and 17/11. Three names with a price in the win contract appear in few lists. François Hollande is 6th on Polymarket, at 3.55, and is at 2.00 on Kalshi; the 3 lists that test him, from 3 pollsters, have fieldwork ending between 15/10 and 22/10 and give him 6.5% to 10%; he is not a declared candidate and, according to Europe 1, has postponed his decision to late January or early February 2027. Christine Lagarde is 4th on Kalshi, at 5.00, and 5th on Polymarket, at 3.95; the two lists that test her are from Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 9 and 10/11, and give her 14% and 8%. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 29/10, the European Central Bank announced that she leaves the bank's presidency on 07/02/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 09/11, is at 0.35 on Polymarket, his lowest price since his series began on 09/11/2026, and at 1.00 on Kalshi; he appears in 5 of the 79 lists, one from each of 5 pollsters, with 2% to 4.5%; in the two most recent, he has 3% in YouGov's and 4% in Ifop's.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are less than one point apart in the poll average; in the Polymarket win contract, Philippe's price is more than three times Glucksmann's.** Philippe averages 11.7 across 24 lists from 6 pollsters with fieldwork ending between 24/10 and 17/11, and Glucksmann 11.2, across 34 lists from 6 pollsters; in the 79 lists from 09/10 to 17/11, Philippe appears in 56 and is among the top two in 3, and Glucksmann appears in 76 and is among the top two in 3. In the win contract, Philippe is at 4.15 on Polymarket, where the series recorded 3.05 at 13:00 UTC on 23/11, his lowest price since 08/11/2026, and at 2.20 on Kalshi; Glucksmann is at 1.15 on Polymarket, his lowest price since 08/11/2026, and at 1.00 on Kalshi.

**In the press collection at 17:00 UTC on 23/11, the ten headlines come from 8 outlets; the runoff date, the election at the Association of Mayors of France and Génération·s's backing of Jean-Luc Mélenchon are among the subjects.** Le Figaro asks whether the government can still change the election date: after Bruno Retailleau, the president of the Senate, Gérard Larcher, and Raphaël Glucksmann, the general secretary of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, asked in an interview with La Tribune Dimanche on 21/11 for the runoff date, May 2, 2027, to be changed because of the risk of tension on the day after May Day ("Il n'y a aucune justification convaincante pour le maintien de cette date", there is no convincing justification for keeping this date); according to ICI, government spokesperson Maud Bregeon ruled out any change in late October. According to BFMTV, Lisnard said he remains a presidential candidate even if he is not re-elected president of the Association of Mayors of France, whose congress runs from 24 to 26/11 in Paris; his only opponent there is Philippe Laurent, mayor of Sceaux. 20 Minutes reports that the Génération·s party, founded by Benoît Hamon, decided to back Mélenchon, with 85% of its members' votes, and reached an agreement for the legislative elections with La France insoumise (LFI); according to Paul Vannier, of LFI, 12 constituencies are set aside for Génération·s. BFMTV reports, citing sources, that Emmanuel Macron said at a dinner with industry leaders in Toulouse: "Je ne suis pas autorisé à faire campagne, autrement je peux vous dire que j'irais" (I am not allowed to campaign, otherwise I can tell you I would). Two headlines are about the withdrawal of François Ruffin's candidacy, announced on 21/11: in Le Parisien, Glucksmann salutes his "combat" (fight), and on TF1 Info the journalist Christophe Barbier analyses the decision. In the Polymarket contract on who will be on the ballot, Ruffin is at 2.65 in the 17:05 UTC reading; he appears in 8 of the 79 first-round lists with fieldwork ending between 09/10 and 17/11, from 4 pollsters, with 1.5% to 3%.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, does not turn price into voting intention and does not show poll figures without the official notice checked. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as required by the French law of 1977.
